title: LangChain raised $300 million to sell control of agents, not a model.
friendlyTitle: LangChain raised $300 million. The product is control of agents, not a model.
summary: On 13 November, LangChain said it raised $300 million at a $3 billion valuation, led by CapitalG. That is more than double the $1.25 billion valuation from about a year ago. The company says more than 7,000 organisations use LangSmith to run, test, and govern agents without locking the work to one model. It also says Workday cut the time to deploy a new agent from five months to under a day. Those customer figures are LangChain's.
friendlySummary: On 13 November, LangChain said investors put $300 million into the company, at a $3 billion price. That is more than double last year's price. The company says more than 7,000 organisations use LangSmith to run and watch agents, and to switch models. It says Workday can now launch an agent in under a day, down from five months. Those numbers come from LangChain.
whyItMatters: The open-source library is no longer the business. If you already run agents, the useful question is whether you can see what they did, swap the model, and stop a tool call. LangChain says it will show new LangSmith features on 20 November. A valuation is not a product review.
friendlyWhyItMatters: The old free library is not the business now. If you use agents, ask whether you can see what they did, change the model, and block a tool. LangChain says it will show new features on 20 November. A high price from investors is not a review of the product.
